title: What Happens on the Internet in One Second?
lines: What happens on the internet in one single second?
It starts with one phone, | lighting up in the dark.
In that same second, | people type more than {100,000~a hundred thousand} searches into Google.
That's over {8 billion~eight billion} questions a day. | And the strangest number comes last.
Zoom out, | and that second also sends {about/~about} {4 million~four million} emails.
Nearly half of them are spam.
Meanwhile, about {8 hours~eight hours} of new video land on YouTube.
Not every minute. | Every second.
All of it has to live somewhere: | in vast warehouses of computers called data centers.
Experts estimate they use about {1.5%~one and a half percent} of all the world's electricity.
Roughly as much as the whole of France.
And to cross from one continent to another, | the data doesn't fly through space.
It goes under the sea.
About {1.4 million kilometers~one point four million kilometers} of cable lie on the ocean floor.
That's enough to wrap around the Earth {35 times.~thirty-five times.}
In the deep sea, | many are about as thick as a garden hose.
Yet they carry more than {99%~ninety-nine percent} of the traffic between continents.
Now, back to that one phone, | and those {8 hours~eight hours} of YouTube every second.
One single day of uploads | would take about {82 years~eighty-two years} to watch, nonstop. | Longer than a lifetime.
What damages undersea internet cables the most? | Shark bites, | or fishing gear and ship anchors? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: More than {99%~ninety-nine percent} of the internet between continents runs under the sea.
